newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN QUIET MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN QUIET MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted largely stable in dull trade on Tuesday.
Local money dealers said most players on the market were reluctant to buy any paper for fear of making losses if rates hardened.
"We're all trying to work out a trend to see where the rates will go from here," one dealer said.

The money rates, which were quoted at around 16 percent a month ago, have surged to around 23 percent, fuelled by market sentiment that they should rise in line with annual inflation, which went up to 19.9 percent in March from 19 percent.
"At the moment people continue to buy treasury bills which are the most attractive paper at the moment," a dealer said on Tuesday.

He said the central bank sold Z$700 million worth of treasury bills to discount houses at 22.94 percent, down from 23 percent the previous day. The bills were being re-sold on the secondary market at a steady 20 percent.

Indicative rates for NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were quoted at 25 and 20 percent (buying and selling respectively) while bankers acceptances were also unchanged at 24 percent (buying) and 20 percent on the sell-side. Call money held steady at 20 percent.
